new_for_file.brief: Creates a new `GtkPicture` displaying the given `file`.
new_for_file.md:
Creates a new `GtkPicture` displaying the given `file`.

If the file isn’t found or can’t be loaded, the resulting
`GtkPicture` is empty.

If you need to detect failures to load the file, use an
image loading framework such as libglycin to load the file
yourself, then create the `GtkPicture` from the texture.

new_for_filename.brief: Creates a new `GtkPicture` displaying the file `filename`.
new_for_filename.md:
Creates a new `GtkPicture` displaying the file `filename`.

This is a utility function that calls [`Picture.new_for_file()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Picture#constructor:new_for_file).
See that function for details.

new_for_paintable.md:
Creates a new `GtkPicture` displaying `paintable`.

The `GtkPicture` will track changes to the `paintable` and update
its size and contents in response to it.

new_for_pixbuf.md:
Creates a new `GtkPicture` displaying `pixbuf`.

This is a utility function that calls [`Picture.new_for_paintable()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Picture#constructor:new_for_paintable),
See that function for details.

The pixbuf must not be modified after passing it to this function.

new_for_resource.brief: Creates a new `GtkPicture` displaying the resource at `resource_path`.
new_for_resource.md:
Creates a new `GtkPicture` displaying the resource at `resource_path`.

This is a utility function that calls [`Picture.new_for_file()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Picture#constructor:new_for_file).
See that function for details.

doc.md:
Displays a `GdkPaintable`.

Many convenience functions are provided to make pictures simple to use.
For example, if you want to load an image from a file, and then display
it, there’s a convenience function to do this:

```c
GtkWidget *widget = gtk_picture_new_for_filename ("myfile.png");
```

If the file isn’t loaded successfully, the picture will contain a
“broken image” icon similar to that used in many web browsers.
If you want to handle errors in loading the file yourself,
for example by displaying an error message, then load the image with
and image loading framework such as libglycin, then create the `GtkPicture`
with [`Picture.new_for_paintable()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Picture#constructor:new_for_paintable).

Sometimes an application will want to avoid depending on external data
files, such as image files. See the documentation of `GResource` for details.
In this case, [`Picture.new_for_resource()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Picture#constructor:new_for_resource) and
[`Picture.set_resource()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Picture#method:set_resource) should be used.

`GtkPicture` displays an image at its natural size. See [`Image`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image)
if you want to display a fixed-size image, such as an icon.

## Sizing the paintable

You can influence how the paintable is displayed inside the `GtkPicture`
by changing [`Picture:content-fit`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Picture#property:content-fit). See [`ContentFit`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ContentFit)
for details. [`Picture:can-shrink`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Picture#property:can-shrink) can be unset to make sure
that paintables are never made smaller than their ideal size - but
be careful if you do not know the size of the paintable in use (like
when displaying user-loaded images). This can easily cause the picture to
grow larger than the screen. And [`Widget:halign`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#property:halign) and
[`Widget:valign`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#property:valign) can be used to make sure the paintable doesn't
fill all available space but is instead displayed at its original size.

## CSS nodes

`GtkPicture` has a single CSS node with the name `picture`.

## Accessibility

`GtkPicture` uses the [`AccessibleRole.img`](xref:gtk:Gtk.AccessibleRole#value:img) role.

get_alternative_text.brief: Gets the alternative textual description of the picture.
get_alternative_text.md:
Gets the alternative textual description of the picture.

The returned string will be `NULL` if the picture cannot be described textually.

get_can_shrink.brief: Returns whether the `GtkPicture` respects its contents size.
get_can_shrink.md: Returns whether the `GtkPicture` respects its contents size.

get_content_fit.brief: Returns the fit mode for the content of the `GtkPicture`.
get_content_fit.md:
Returns the fit mode for the content of the `GtkPicture`.

See [`ContentFit`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ContentFit) for details.

get_file.brief: Gets the `GFile` currently displayed if `self` is displaying a file.
get_file.md:
Gets the `GFile` currently displayed if `self` is displaying a file.

If `self` is not displaying a file, for example when
[`Picture.set_paintable()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Picture#method:set_paintable) was used, then `NULL` is returned.

get_isolate_contents.brief: Returns whether the contents are isolated.
get_isolate_contents.md: Returns whether the contents are isolated.

get_keep_aspect_ratio.brief: Returns whether the `GtkPicture` preserves its contents aspect ratio.
get_keep_aspect_ratio.deprecated_md:
Use [`Picture.get_content_fit()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Picture#method:get_content_fit) instead. This will
  now return `FALSE` only if [`Picture:content-fit`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Picture#property:content-fit) is
  `GTK_CONTENT_FIT_FILL`. Returns `TRUE` otherwise.
get_keep_aspect_ratio.md: Returns whether the `GtkPicture` preserves its contents aspect ratio.

get_paintable.brief: Gets the `GdkPaintable` being displayed by the `GtkPicture`.
get_paintable.md: Gets the `GdkPaintable` being displayed by the `GtkPicture`.

set_alternative_text.brief: Sets an alternative textual description for the picture contents.
set_alternative_text.md:
Sets an alternative textual description for the picture contents.

It is equivalent to the "alt" attribute for images on websites.

This text will be made available to accessibility tools.

If the picture cannot be described textually, set this property to `NULL`.

set_can_shrink.brief: If set to `TRUE`, then `self` can be made smaller than its contents.
set_can_shrink.md:
If set to `TRUE`, then `self` can be made smaller than its contents.

The contents will then be scaled down when rendering.

If you want to still force a minimum size manually, consider using
[`Widget.set_size_request()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:set_size_request).

Also of note is that a similar function for growing does not exist
because the grow behavior can be controlled via
[`Widget.set_halign()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:set_halign) and [`Widget.set_valign()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:set_valign).

set_content_fit.brief: Sets how the content should be resized to fit the `GtkPicture`.
set_content_fit.md:
Sets how the content should be resized to fit the `GtkPicture`.

See [`ContentFit`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ContentFit) for details.

set_file.md:
Makes `self` load and display `file`.

See [`Picture.new_for_file()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Picture#constructor:new_for_file) for details.

::: warning
    Note that this function should not be used with untrusted data.
    Use a proper image loading framework such as libglycin, which can
    load many image formats into a `GdkTexture`, and then use
    [`Image.set_from_paintable()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#method:set_from_paintable).

set_filename.brief: Makes `self` load and display the given `filename`.
set_filename.md:
Makes `self` load and display the given `filename`.

This is a utility function that calls [`Picture.set_file()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Picture#method:set_file).

::: warning
    Note that this function should not be used with untrusted data.
    Use a proper image loading framework such as libglycin, which can
    load many image formats into a `GdkTexture`, and then use
    [`Image.set_from_paintable()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#method:set_from_paintable).

set_isolate_contents.brief: If set to true, then the contents will be rendered individually.
set_isolate_contents.md:
If set to true, then the contents will be rendered individually.

If set to false they will be able to erase or otherwise mix with
the background.

GTK supports finer grained isolation, in rare cases where you need
this, you can use [`Snapshot.push_isolation()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Snapshot#method:push_isolation) yourself to
achieve this.

By default contents are isolated.

set_keep_aspect_ratio.brief: If set to `TRUE`, the `self` will render its contents according to their aspect ratio.
set_keep_aspect_ratio.deprecated_md:
Use [`Picture.set_content_fit()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Picture#method:set_content_fit) instead. If still
  used, this method will always set the [`Picture:content-fit`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Picture#property:content-fit)
  property to `GTK_CONTENT_FIT_CONTAIN` if `keep_aspect_ratio` is true,
  otherwise it will set it to `GTK_CONTENT_FIT_FILL`.
set_keep_aspect_ratio.md:
If set to `TRUE`, the `self` will render its contents according to
their aspect ratio.

That means that empty space may show up at the top/bottom or
left/right of `self`.

If set to `FALSE` or if the contents provide no aspect ratio,
the contents will be stretched over the picture's whole area.

set_paintable.md:
Makes `self` display the given `paintable`.

If `paintable` is `NULL`, nothing will be displayed.

See [`Picture.new_for_paintable()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Picture#constructor:new_for_paintable) for details.

set_pixbuf.md:
Sets a `GtkPicture` to show a `GdkPixbuf`.

See [`Picture.new_for_pixbuf()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Picture#constructor:new_for_pixbuf) for details.

This is a utility function that calls [`Picture.set_paintable()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Picture#method:set_paintable).

set_resource.brief: Makes `self` load and display the resource at the given `resource_path`.
set_resource.md:
Makes `self` load and display the resource at the given
`resource_path`.

This is a utility function that calls [`Picture.set_file()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Picture#method:set_file).
